context.content: (Off-topic/meta.) Interestingly, my (h-)feed reader displays a (p-)name for this “note.” Normally, it drops the p-name (and thus considers the post a “note”) if it’s the same as (or a shortened version of) the content. In this case it doesn’t, because this post’s p-name contains a straight quote whereas in the content it’s a “curly” quote. Which raises the question: Why add the p-name class at all, if this a note?

replies.content: Had a few interesting discussions lately on missing titles from RSS/Atom feeds—seems some readers are still expecting a title for each and every post. In that case, having the title be a (truncated) copy of the content usually works okay, as, e.g., Aperture will (usually) correctly recognize (and drop) them. For h-feed specifically, though, I don’t see the need for a p-name at all—only “IndieWeb” readers actually support h-feed, and they (obviously) display “notes” just fine.
